top.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
top.summary: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.

more.title: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive
more.summary: Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually just by turning food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades largely driven by population growth. Unlike fossil fuel emissions, however, the CO2 we exhale is part of the natural carbon cycle, and scientists say measuring it more accurately could improve climate models.

more.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
more.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.

more.title: Personalized savings reminders can help boost retirement savings

more.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station

more.title: The hidden ways insects support animal life—from habitat to health—go way beyond being food
more.summary: There are at least 14 million insect species on Earth, and they play highly diverse roles in sustaining the natural world. Insects provide many well-known benefits—what scientists often call "ecosystem services." For example, you can thank a bee or a hoverfly for pollinating wildflowers and agricultural crops, or credit dung beetles for decomposing manure and other waste materials.

more.title: Different text genres help doctoral students adapt their writing to reach new readers
more.summary: An academic abstract, a blog post and a public outreach article all place different demands on the writer. Readers' prior knowledge varies, as does the purpose of the text and what needs explaining. Mastering one kind of text therefore does not automatically mean being able to write another.

more.title: Earth's gravity may have kept the early moon's volcanic heart beating
more.summary: We typically think of the moon as a static, floating object that has remained the same for basically its entire lifetime, with an occasional asteroid impact serving as an exception. That understanding is grounded in physics—the moon should have cooled rapidly after forming when a huge protoplanet hit the early Earth around 4.5 billion years ago.

more.title: Heavy rain can more than double glacier speeds in Alaska
more.summary: Glaciers are often thought of as unyielding blocks of ice that slowly carve out the landscape as they move downhill by gravity. But sometimes their slow crawl becomes a surge that sees them move orders of magnitude faster than their usual speed.

more.title: The introduction of a medieval public health system exposed the population to roundworm

more.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
